title: GO execution context and address resolver wave

remainingExcludedWork: general per-component dispatcher beyond the bootstrap attachment

nativeHarness: stale attachment rejection before engine-pointer reads
500000 warmed iterations across all nine structured routes with zero generated C++ allocations
implementedEvidence.boundary: The bootstrap attachment supplies a real engine context. Generated .script.ts per-instance dispatch remains a separate implementation frontier.

findings.finding: Exact relative receiver resolution requires the full sender URL including component fragment. The generic payload is bounded to 2 KiB and needs generated DDF plus generic-table codecs. dmMessage::Post and dmDDF descriptor lookup are public, but the engine message queue may allocate pages on first use or overflow.

The public CompFactorySpawn path can avoid Lua. Failure returns nil, so the sound TypeScript result is DefoldHash | undefined. Default position, rotation, and scale come from the sender instance. Child initialization is synchronous and must push then restore the parent active context.

The public game-object APIs support a Lua-free route. Deletion is deferred until the end of the frame, so deleting the current instance must not invalidate its active callback context early. Single-target and list missing-target behavior differ and remain explicit semantic tokens.

Exact lookup returns a private NodeProxy carrying scene and HNode. Public dmSDK lacks exact lookup and validity operations. A portable plugin therefore needs a generated Lua fallback or a focused upstream dmSDK addition; private symbol declarations are forbidden.

Exact node validation and text mutation are not public dmSDK. Number input follows Lua %.14g formatting, and the engine inherently frees then duplicates text on each call. Scene-bound generation-tagged handles are required for any bridge token.

verifiedIntegrationGaps.finding: The present adapter stores one instanceRef and attach replaces it. That model cannot prove correct current-instance behavior for multiple player, rocket, and GUI component instances or reentrant callbacks.

Generated proxies call attachComponent, dispatchLifecycle, dispatchInput, dispatchMessage, and detachComponent, while the inspected extension registration only exposes attach. This proposal assumes a future component dispatcher and does not claim it exists.
ScriptCallFrame carries values and scratch only. The smallest design is a native scoped context stack owned by the component dispatcher, not a raw native pointer exposed to JavaScript.

generatorProposal.noHandAuthoredPerApiLogic: Per-binding thunks must be selected from structured metadata and small reusable terminal operations. Source-derived semantic exceptions must be explicit data records with citations.

activeScope.entry: Every generated Lua proxy callback enters native code while Defold has already set its current Lua script instance. The component dispatcher obtains the current HInstance with public dmScript::CheckGOInstance(L), then pushes a native RAII context scope before invoking Hermes.
activeScope.exit: The scope pops on success, JavaScript exception, Lua error conversion, nested dispatch, and early return.
activeScope.reentrancy: A bounded or arena-backed stack is required. A single global current instance and a single replaceable registry reference are forbidden for component dispatch.
activeScope.threading: Context is engine-thread scoped. No HInstance pointer may be transferred to a worker or retained by JavaScript.

lifetime.synchronous: currentInstance is borrowed only for the synchronous proxy-to-Hermes call extent
lifetime.asynchronous: timer or deferred callback stores an attachment handle, then re-resolves identifier in the collection and validates both attachment generation and game-object generation before pushing a scope
lifetime.detach: final/detach invalidates the attachment generation and releases any Lua registry reference before JavaScript state can be reused

addressResolverContract.name: GameObjectAddressResolver

acceptedVariants.sourceParity: ResolveInstance defaults to the current instance when the argument is absent or nil

acceptedVariants.result: parse [socket:][path][#fragment], resolve a relative path against currentInstance, then select the URL path
notes: A component fragment is ignored for GO instance selection after URL parsing.
The current source accepts Lua strings, therefore embedded NUL behavior is NUL-terminated in downstream C-string operations.

acceptedVariants.result: current collection socket plus hash as the path and fragment zero
copy URL POD, then use its socket and path

algorithm: Normalize omitted, undefined, and raw-runtime null to current instance; generated TypeScript continues to expose only an optional argument.
For string, parse URL syntax. Resolve relative path with dmGameObject::GetAbsoluteIdentifier(currentInstance, path). Preserve explicit absolute path hashing and socket lookup semantics.
For hash, use it directly as the instance path in currentCollection.
For URL, copy the fixed-layout value.
Reject missing instances before calling an engine terminal operation.

result.allocation: none for omitted, hash, or URL; string route is designed for bounded stack parsing and must prove no heap allocation after warm-up

policyDifferencesToRecord.sourceBehavior: Extra arguments can cause ResolveInstance to keep the current instance because it tests exact Lua stack arity.
policyDifferencesToRecord.generatedPolicy: Reject arguments outside generated call shapes before resolution. Do not emulate undocumented extra-argument behavior.

policyDifferencesToRecord.sourceBehavior: Explicit nil chooses the current instance.
policyDifferencesToRecord.generatedPolicy: TypeScript exposes an optional address. Raw JavaScript null and undefined may normalize to omitted for parity, but that must be tested and documented.

adjacentBlockerMatrix.whyAdjacent: All three bindings depend on the exact currently executing player or rocket instance.
adjacentBlockerMatrix.minimumContract: Proxy entry pushes a per-attachment ActiveGameObjectContext around the synchronous Hermes call; nested entries restore the previous context.
adjacentBlockerMatrix.mustNotAssume: The most recently attached component is the current component.

adjacentBlockerMatrix.whyAdjacent: The shared address union accepts hash, and War Battles passes message.otherId to go.delete and compares hashed action/message identifiers.
adjacentBlockerMatrix.currentEvidence: Resolved after this design snapshot: generated_script_value_bindings.cpp carries all 64 bits in a POD handle payload and JavaScript exposes a branded bigint.

adjacentBlockerMatrix.whyAdjacent: It removes the heterogeneous-union blocker for the three GO transforms and is reused by msg.post, factory.create, and go.delete.

adjacentBlockerMatrix.deferredComplexity: Address arrays, recursive boolean overload, bone rejection, and asynchronous stale-handle semantics are a separate lifecycle terminal pattern.

adjacentBlockerMatrix.whyAdjacent: Uses the same sender context and address codec, but payload encoding and queue allocation are separate from GO transform terminals.
adjacentBlockerMatrix.deferredComplexity: DDF versus generic table wire codecs and the 2048-byte bound.

hotPathTargets: current-instance getPosition: zero Lua allocator calls and zero C++ heap calls after initialization
current-instance setPosition/setRotation: zero Lua allocator calls and zero C++ heap calls after initialization
hash/URL addressed variants: zero allocations after initialization

allocationAndCachePolicy.scratch: Any call-local resolver scratch is scoped by a reentrant BindingArena frame. Nested Hermes-to-engine-to-Hermes calls receive nested frames and cannot overwrite parent scratch.
allocationAndCachePolicy.cache: A per-attachment optional address cache may key on exact UTF-8 bytes and collection identity, but cached targets must store identifier plus generation, not an unchecked HInstance pointer.
notCountedAsAllocationFree: Lua registry reference creation for fallback
engine allocations caused by unrelated component behavior

realEngineProofMatrix.setup: Create two game objects with the same generated TypeScript component and distinct initial local positions.
realEngineProofMatrix.stimulus: Each update calls go.getPosition() and reports its value through a deterministic native transcript.
realEngineProofMatrix.requiredObservation: Each component observes its own position on every alternating update; neither observes the most recently attached instance.

realEngineProofMatrix.setup: Place a TypeScript-controlled child under a translated, rotated, and scaled parent.
realEngineProofMatrix.stimulus: TypeScript reads local position, sets a new local position, and a Lua verifier reads go.get_position and go.get_world_position in the same frame.
realEngineProofMatrix.requiredObservation: TypeScript and Lua local values match component-wise at float32 precision; world value differs according to the parent transform.

realEngineProofMatrix.setup: Place a TypeScript-controlled child under a rotated parent.
realEngineProofMatrix.stimulus: TypeScript sets a non-normalized finite quaternion and a Lua verifier reads local and world rotations.
realEngineProofMatrix.requiredObservation: Local quaternion matches the supplied float32 components without generator normalization; world rotation includes the parent transform.

realEngineProofMatrix.setup: Create caller and target instances inside a nested collection path.
realEngineProofMatrix.stimulus: Call all three bindings using a relative string and an absolute string for the same target.
realEngineProofMatrix.requiredObservation: Both routes resolve the intended target and agree with Lua GO calls.

realEngineProofMatrix.setup: Obtain an absolute target hash without converting it through JavaScript number.
realEngineProofMatrix.stimulus: Read and mutate the target using the hash address variant.
realEngineProofMatrix.requiredObservation: All 64 bits survive and the exact target is selected.

realEngineProofMatrix.layer: native ABI harness then Defold native executable when URL production is executable
realEngineProofMatrix.setup: Supply a fixed-layout URL value whose socket and path identify a same-collection target.
realEngineProofMatrix.stimulus: Read and mutate through the URL variant.
realEngineProofMatrix.requiredObservation: URL bytes are copied, fragment does not change selected game object, and no pointer escapes the call.

realEngineProofMatrix.setup: Load a second collection socket and construct its target URL.
realEngineProofMatrix.stimulus: Call each GO transform binding from the first collection against the second collection URL.
realEngineProofMatrix.requiredObservation: Each call fails before the terminal dmGameObject operation; the current instance and Lua stack remain intact; a following valid call succeeds.

realEngineProofMatrix.setup: Construct a valid same-collection path that has no live instance.
realEngineProofMatrix.stimulus: Call each GO transform binding with it.
realEngineProofMatrix.requiredObservation: Each fails deterministically and no engine terminal call is recorded; the next valid call succeeds.

realEngineProofMatrix.layer: native ABI harness and Defold native executable
realEngineProofMatrix.setup: Prepare wrong Defold value kinds and vector/quaternion values containing NaN.
realEngineProofMatrix.requiredObservation: Wrong kinds and NaN are rejected before engine mutation. Infinity behavior is recorded separately because pinned Lua checks reject NaN but not infinity.

realEngineProofMatrix.layer: Defold native executable after component dispatcher and factory.create are executable
realEngineProofMatrix.setup: Object A spawns object B; B init calls GO transforms synchronously before A resumes.
realEngineProofMatrix.stimulus: A reads before spawn, B mutates itself in init, then A mutates itself after spawn returns.
realEngineProofMatrix.requiredObservation: B operations target B and the post-spawn A operation targets A.

realEngineProofMatrix.layer: Defold native executable after deferred callback support exists
realEngineProofMatrix.setup: Capture an async callback in a component, delete/finalize that component, and create another object that may reuse storage.
realEngineProofMatrix.stimulus: Attempt to fire the old callback.
realEngineProofMatrix.requiredObservation: Attachment generation rejects the callback before HInstance dereference and the new object is not mutated.

realEngineProofMatrix.layer: native harness plus instrumented Defold native executable
realEngineProofMatrix.setup: Warm descriptor lookup, context attachment, and all address variants; install Lua allocator and C++ allocation counters around the measured region.
realEngineProofMatrix.stimulus: Run at least 10000 current-instance getPosition/setPosition/setRotation calls, then hash and URL addressed variants.
realEngineProofMatrix.requiredObservation: Zero Lua allocator calls and zero C++ heap calls in direct binding code; stable Lua stack height; stable context depth; no scratch high-water growth after warm-up.

realEngineProofMatrix.setup: Reuse the two-instance and local transform fixture under the browser-host JavaScript route.
realEngineProofMatrix.requiredObservation: Transcript matches native within declared float32 tolerance and context isolation remains correct.

acceptanceGates: The generator emits all three primary stable IDs from structured IR plus explicit semantic metadata.
No per-function handwritten switch is required outside reusable terminal operation selection.
Every generated route rejects absence of ActiveGameObjectContext.
All current-instance and hash/URL probes pass on a real Defold native executable.
String, cross-collection, missing-target, and post-error recovery probes pass.
The reentrant A-to-B-to-A probe passes before factory.create is called executable.
Allocation claims are made only after counter evidence, never from code inspection alone.
The runtime gate changes an API to generatedDispatch=true only after its real-engine probe evidence is recorded.

recommendedOrder.deliverable: Per-invocation ActiveGameObjectContext stack in the component dispatcher
recommendedOrder.reason: Without it direct GO calls can silently target the wrong object even if terminal calls are correct.

recommendedOrder.deliverable: Current-instance-only thunks for getPosition, setPosition, and setRotation
recommendedOrder.reason: This matches every War Battles use of these APIs and proves the context contract with the smallest surface. It is a fixture milestone, not full API completion.

recommendedOrder.deliverable: Shared string/hash/URL resolver and full optional-address call shapes
recommendedOrder.reason: This completes the documented three APIs and becomes reusable input infrastructure for delete, msg.post, and factory.create.
They validate lifecycle safety before expanding to spawn, delete, timers, and messages.

openQuestions.question: Should URL receive a dedicated fixed-layout ScriptValue payload or a call-local data pointer plus size?
openQuestions.decisionConstraint: All three 64-bit URL fields must survive Static Hermes, dynamic Hermes, and browser-host bridges without JavaScript-number truncation.

openQuestions.question: Should raw JavaScript null be accepted as omitted for parity with explicit Lua nil?
openQuestions.decisionConstraint: Generated TypeScript need not expose null even if runtime parity accepts it.

openQuestions.question: Is address caching worth its invalidation complexity for string targets?
openQuestions.decisionConstraint: No unchecked HInstance pointer may be cached across frames; identifier and generation must be validated.
